1.why: All screenshots show a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing on headings, body text, and labels.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, all-caps, or dense paragraphs across every step.

3.why: The centered card layout, large form fields, and stacked buttons appear well adapted and readable for a mobile viewport.

4.why: Copy such as “Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone” is short and in plain language.

5.why: The phone field provides a placeholder example (+447700900000), but the email and verification-code fields show no example format.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block of text; all instructional copy is only one or two brief sentences.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control is present for the verification code; the user must type it manually.

8.why: No QR code or other non-manual alternative for entering the code appears in any screenshot.

9.why: Screenshots give no visible evidence (e.g., autofill styling or password-manager UI) that browser autofill is supported.

10.why: “Step X of 3” label and the prominent solid blue primary button make the current step and main action stand out clearly.

11.why: Each screen requests only a single primary action—enter credentials or enter the verification code.

12.why: The error banner only says “We could not complete that request. Please try again,” without plainly stating what happened or what comes next.

13.why: Retry is possible on the same form and “Use different details” exists, yet no reveal/hide or re-request-code controls are shown.

14.why: The error message is generic, does not name the concrete problem, and gives only “Please try again” as guidance, though it avoids blame.

15.why: No reading time limit is imposed, but the code explicitly expires in 10 minutes, which is only moderately generous for entry.
